a2112.speech: Claimed that his life was in danger and maintains that the criminal charges against him (unlawful possession of a firearm, receiving stolen property and procuring the registration of a firearm by false pretence) are a political witchhunt by the Masisi regime; also claimed that the government was using State security organs such as the DIS to target him following his fallout with Masisi.

a2112.speaker: Ian Khama, former President of Botswana
a2112.name: Ian Khama
a2112.title: former President of Botswana
a2112.speech: Responded that there is absolutely no doubt in his mind that the regime will continue to persecute him: "Even at this moment since my return, the DIS has been keeping me under surveillance everywhere I go. This is what they did before I left the country in order to plan an event that would cause me harm."

a2112.speaker: Ian Khama, former President of Botswana
a2112.name: Ian Khama
a2112.title: former President of Botswana
a2112.speech: "No I was not concerned about an Interpol red notice because none existed. As such, no arrest could have been effected under the circumstances you describe."

a2112.speaker: Government of Botswana and the Directorate of Intelligence and Security (DIS)
a2112.name: Government of Botswana and the Directorate of Intelligence and Security (DIS)
a2112.speech: Have on numerous occasions denied that it was targeting the former president.

a2112.speaker: Dumezweni Mthimkhulu, late former Minister of Environment and Tourism of Botswana
a2112.name: Dumezweni Mthimkhulu
a2112.title: late former Minister of Environment and Tourism of Botswana
a2112.speech: Urged authorities in the United Kingdom, while he was in London in March, to lobby the British Parliament against passing the Hunting Trophies (Import Prohibition) Bill.

a2112.speaker: Dumezweni Mthimkhulu, late former Minister of Environment and Tourism of Botswana
a2112.name: Dumezweni Mthimkhulu
a2112.title: late former Minister of Environment and Tourism of Botswana
a2112.speech: Told the UK lawmakers that the ex-head of state was a fugitive from the law in Botswana.

a2136.speaker: U.S. Embassy in Burundi
a2136.name: U.S. Embassy in Burundi
a2136.speech: Announced new funding of USD $796,000 to revitalize the country's agricultural sector and empower local farmers, supporting a five-year initiative, "Resilient Food Systems and Improved Local Sourcing through Private Sector-Led Market Access for Job Creation," part of USAID's Economic Recovery and Reform Activity (USAID-ERRA).

a2136.speaker: Dr. Aliou Tall, Acting Country Representative for USAID Burundi
a2136.name: Dr. Aliou Tall
a2136.title: Acting Country Representative for USAID Burundi
a2136.speech: "The investments in agriculture and food security are critical for ensuring sustainable development in Burundi." ; "The partnerships we're fostering between public institutions, private sector actors, and development organizations underscore our commitment to unlocking Burundi's full potential."

a2182.speaker: Joao Cravinho, new European Union Special Representative for the Sahel
a2182.name: Joao Cravinho
a2182.title: new European Union Special Representative for the Sahel
a2182.speech: received on Monday by Nigerien Prime Minister Ali Mahaman Lamine Zeine, the European diplomat spoke of "great opportunities for the future" and insisted on the need for "mutual understanding" ; he says he shares with the Nigerien authorities the "will to turn the page."

a2182.speaker: Tele Sahel
a2182.name: Tele Sahel
a2182.speech: reported the visit to Niamey of the new EU Special Representative for the Sahel, Joao Cravinho, which marks a first attempt at rapprochement after the diplomatic crisis that culminated in November with the departure of the European ambassador.

a2182.speaker: Nigerien Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a2182.name: Nigerien Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a2182.speech: denounced an "unsolicited" aid, distributed "in total opacity" through NGOs, while the government intended to manage the situation with its own funds; the authorities particularly reproached the ambassador for having proceeded "unilaterally" with the allocation of the grant to several organisations, notably the ICRC (banned from operating in Niger), the DRC and COOPI, denouncing an "arbitrary" distribution of funds by region.

a2182.speaker: Brussels (European Union)
a2182.name: Brussels (European Union)
a2182.speech: expressed "its profound disagreement with the allegations", maintaining that humanitarian aid was provided "in a neutral, impartial and independent manner" through UN agencies and international organisations.

a2182.speaker: Government of Niger (Niamey)
a2182.name: Government of Niger (Niamey)
a2182.speech: asserted that unauthorised operations had continued despite the ambassador being summoned in October and given an explicit warning; Niamey launched an audit of the management of the funds and formally asked the EU to do the same, and presented the departure of EU ambassador Salvador Pinto Da Franca as being on its own initiative.

a2401.speaker: Situmbeko Musokotwane, Zambian Finance and National Planning Minister
a2401.name: Situmbeko Musokotwane
a2401.title: Zambian Finance and National Planning Minister
a2401.speech: Says it has been tough dealing with the abruptness of the cut in the United States’ funding to the health sector, and that it would have been better to be told two years earlier; admitted that donor aid cannot last forever but criticised the manner of the withdrawal. “It’s been tough dealing with the abruptness of the cut. Of course, everyone knows that aid is not meant to last forever, and at some point we have to become less aid-dependent. But what’s been difficult is how suddenly it’s being implemented. It would have been better to be told two, three, or even four years ahead – but that didn’t happen.”

a2401.speaker: Situmbeko Musokotwane, Zambian Finance and National Planning Minister
a2401.name: Situmbeko Musokotwane
a2401.title: Zambian Finance and National Planning Minister
a2401.speech: Noted that the tough US tariffs would hurt Zambia as an exporter of copper ; ruled out cutting ties with the US, insisting that “we will not disengage from US because of this. There are problems but we are hopeful this can be resolved.”

a2401.speaker: Situmbeko Musokotwane, Zambian Finance and National Planning Minister
a2401.name: Situmbeko Musokotwane
a2401.title: Zambian Finance and National Planning Minister
a2401.speech: Has called for a fundamental shift in how the country approaches its mining sector, stressing the urgent need to increase mineral production, and reminded delegates that national prosperity hinges on growth in output – not the preservation of outdated systems. “If we are going to create environments that benefit many people, that only happens when we produce more and more.” ; “This country will not become wealthy if we keep producing copper in the same quantity as we did in 1964,” he warned.

a2413.speaker: Baroness Blower, Vice-Chair of the APPG on Global Education (chair of the event)
a2413.name: Baroness Blower
a2413.title: Vice-Chair of the APPG on Global Education (chair of the event)
a2413.speech: "Foundational skills... are the building blocks of reaping the full benefits of education. These figures are not just numbers and percentages. They represent lost opportunity, stalled progress, and unjust barriers to the next generation."

a2413.speaker: Ministers from Ghana, Zambia, Sierra Leone, Malawi, Zimbabwe, South Africa and Uganda
a2413.name: Ministers from Ghana
a2413.title: Zambia, Sierra Leone, Malawi, Zimbabwe, South Africa and Uganda
a2413.speech: Shared how targeted investments - particularly in early years teaching, local language instruction, and structured pedagogy - are delivering measurable results.

a2413.speaker: What Works Hub for Global Education (new research)
a2413.name: What Works Hub for Global Education (new research)
a2413.speech: New research demonstrates the profound economic consequences of not investing in education - and the tremendous opportunity presented by addressing it.

a2413.speaker: Dr. Ben Piper, Director of Global Education at the Gates Foundation
a2413.name: Dr. Ben Piper
a2413.title: Director of Global Education at the Gates Foundation
a2413.speech: Stressed the cost-effectiveness of investments in foundational learning, showing that programmes focused on early learning deliver 3x the impact, 10x the reach, at 1,000th of the cost of standard interventions in high-income countries ; "This is an unsolved problem that has a solution. There's so much work in health to make sure that [children] survive past birth, past some of the early challenges, but we also want them to thrive. Its through programmes on foundational learning and efforts of partners in the room that we do that."

a2413.speaker: Judith Herbertson, Head of Girls' Education at the UK's Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office
a2413.name: Judith Herbertson
a2413.title: Head of Girls' Education at the UK's Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office
a2413.speech: Emphasised findings from the UK co-funded What Works Hub: "Evidence of the return from foundational learning continues to grow.. Children with better foundational learning outcomes are 63% less likely to drop out between the ages of 12 and 15. Women with these basic literacy skills later in life are up to 67% less likely to lose one of their children before the age of five. And an increase of one standard deviation in student test scores is linked to a 2% increase in a country's GDP and a 5% point reduction in youth unemployment."

a2413.speaker: Hon. Siviwe Gwarube, Minister of Basic Education for South Africa
a2413.name: Hon. Siviwe Gwarube
a2413.title: Minister of Basic Education for South Africa
a2413.speech: The key to unlocking the so-called 'demographic dividend' lies in education. Our youth population is not going to automatically be an economic asset. It becomes one when the youth are healthy, when they are skilled and when they are meaningfully engaged in the economy and society. That transformation we believe, begins in our classrooms and literacy and numeracy are the foundation upon which all future learning is built.

a2413.speaker: Hon. Douglas Munsaka Syakalima, Minister of Education for Zambia
a2413.name: Hon. Douglas Munsaka Syakalima
a2413.title: Minister of Education for Zambia
a2413.speech: "Our President is a Champion of Foundational Learning... As he says, the best economic policy is education - the second is education, and the hundredth is education."

a2413.speaker: Ruth Kagia, former Kenyan Minister, High-Level Envoy and Adviser for the Global Partnership for Education
a2413.name: Ruth Kagia
a2413.title: former Kenyan Minister, High-Level Envoy and Adviser for the Global Partnership for Education
a2413.speech: Underscored the critical role the UK has historically played: "When leadership comes from countries themselves, it's easier for partners to rally around them. The UK has been a leader in this space, not just with ideas but with the funding to back them. We hope that leadership doesn't disappear."

a2413.speaker: Halil Dundar, Global Practice Manager at the World Bank
a2413.name: Halil Dundar
a2413.title: Global Practice Manager at the World Bank
a2413.speech: Noted the importance of UK expertise: "FCDO's support, especially in technical engagement, has been vital for delivering results at the country level. In places like Ghana, Sierra Leone, and Ethiopia, we've been able to co-create large-scale education programmes with impact - thanks in part to UK support."

a2413.speaker: Hon. Haruna Iddrisu MP, Minister of Education for Ghana
a2413.name: Hon. Haruna Iddrisu MP
a2413.title: Minister of Education for Ghana
a2413.speech: "We are concerned about the dwindling support and resources of the Western world, including the United States and the British government. That will be a vacuum."

a2413.speaker: Hon. Madalitso Kambauwa Wirima MP, Minister of Education for Malawi
a2413.name: Hon. Madalitso Kambauwa Wirima MP
a2413.title: Minister of Education for Malawi
a2413.speech: Emphasised that this loss of support was happening at a critical time: "It is as if all the partners have withdrawn support at a time when we are building momentum and scaling up what works. We really feel like we are going in the right direction...The timing is not good at all, neither is the global economic outlook. Nonetheless, foundational learning must not only survive, but thrive in this space, because strengthening the human capital foundation for the prosperity of our nation and the world is mandatory."

a2413.speaker: Hon. Douglas Munsaka Syakalima MP, Minister of Education for Zambia
a2413.name: Hon. Douglas Munsaka Syakalima MP
a2413.title: Minister of Education for Zambia
a2413.speech: "This is a wake-up call for us to fill the void. However, there is no question that there will still be gaps in foundational learning outcomes across the world, and that must be justification for the UK to reconsider this decision [to cut ODA] and invest and prioritise education."

a2413.speaker: Lord Jeremy Purvis, Liberal Democrat Spokesperson for Foreign Affairs in the House of Lords
a2413.name: Lord Jeremy Purvis
a2413.title: Liberal Democrat Spokesperson for Foreign Affairs in the House of Lords
a2413.speech: Asked Ministers for advice on how he should make the case to the UK Government to reconsider.

a2413.speaker: Participants in the roundtable
a2413.name: Participants in the roundtable
a2413.speech: Offered compelling arguments for why the UK should remain invested in foundational learning: funding for education is an investment, not aid; education has immense growth potential for the whole globe; foundational skills are not an Africa problem, but a world problem; the immense number of youth in Africa will be a resource for the UK, and the UK stands to gain from a skilled African workforce; education is essential for development - where would Europe be without investment in education? The UK cannot support developing countries to grow socio-economically without investing in education. Several participants emphasised an urgent need for the UK to reassess its plans to deprioritise education.

a2413.speaker: Hon. Conrad Sackey, Minister of Basic and Senior Secondary Education for Sierra Leone
a2413.name: Hon. Conrad Sackey
a2413.title: Minister of Basic and Senior Secondary Education for Sierra Leone
a2413.speech: "We are trying to reduce our reliance on external aid, which is why we've committed this amount of funding. But we have 1 million additional pupils in our system [due to expanding access]... We also are coping with climate change. So we cannot yet wean ourselves completely off external funding, but we are showing bold and great steps to make sure that we contribute to our development."

a2413.speaker: Joseph Nhan-O'Reilly, Director of the International Parliamentary Network for Education
a2413.name: Joseph Nhan-O'Reilly
a2413.title: Director of the International Parliamentary Network for Education
a2413.speech: In closing remarks, reflected on the costs the UK's backtracking will have and shared disappointment in the UK's decision to turn its back on an issue it has long placed at the centre of its development agenda: "There is no healthy society, there is no democratic society, there is no economic growth if our citizens can't read and write and numerate." ; "At a time when the UK has invited all of you here to the Education World Forum, we aren't able to front up and deliver with the support that's necessary....I speak on behalf of MPs who are in the UK Parliament and urging the government to reconsider as well."

a2429.speaker: Dr Billy Grills Harry, National President of the Petroleum Products Retail Outlets Owners Association of Nigeria (PETROAN)
a2429.name: Dr Billy Grills Harry
a2429.title: National President of the Petroleum Products Retail Outlets Owners Association of Nigeria (PETROAN)
a2429.speech: Has raised concerns, in a statement issued in Port Harcourt on Thursday, that approximately 500,000 barrels of crude oil per day allocated for domestic refining often found their way to the international market; commended the federal government for banning the exportation of crude oil allocated to local refineries; said the move is expected to boost local refining capacity, reduce the importation of refined petroleum products, and ease pressure on foreign exchange supply; said the exportation of crude oil meant for domestic refining has led to the abandonment of local refineries and has been a major racketeering scheme, with producers and traders prioritising quick foreign exchange proceeds over local refining ; “Approximately 500,000 barrels of crude oil per day are allocated for domestic refining, but these volumes often find their way to the international market.” ; “The ban is expected to have a positive impact on the economy, as refining crude oil locally will enrich the petrochemical industries and agricultural sector, reduce inequalities in income, and enable Nigeria to transition from a raw material supplier to a value-added product supplier.”

a2429.speaker: Dr Billy Grills Harry, National President of PETROAN
a2429.name: Dr Billy Grills Harry
a2429.title: National President of PETROAN
a2429.speech: Urged the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) to take swift action against refineries, cargo vessels, and companies that default on this policy.

a2444.speaker: Xi Jinping, Chinese President
a2444.name: Xi Jinping
a2444.title: Chinese President
a2444.speech: Put forward the principles of China's Africa policy – sincerity, real results, amity and good faith, and pursuing the greater good and shared interests – charting the course for China's cooperation with Africa and providing the fundamental guidelines.

a2444.speaker: Xi Jinping, Chinese President, and African leaders
a2444.name: Xi Jinping
a2444.title: Chinese President, and African leaders
a2444.speech: Unanimously decided at the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation (FOCAC) Beijing Summit that the two sides would work to build an even stronger China-Africa community of shared future and advance cooperation under the Belt and Road Initiative.

a2444.speaker: China (government position)
a2444.name: China (government position)
a2444.speech: States that in developing relations with Africa there are five lines it will not cross: no interference in African countries' choice of a development path that fits their national conditions; no interference in African countries' internal affairs; no imposition of its will on African countries; no attachment of political strings to assistance to Africa; and no pursuit of selfish political gains through investment and financing cooperation with Africa.

a2444.speaker: China and Africa (FOCAC Beijing Summit 2018 agreement)
a2444.name: China and Africa (FOCAC Beijing Summit 2018 agreement)
a2444.speech: Reached a strategic agreement to build a China-Africa community of shared future characterized by joint responsibility, win-win cooperation, happiness for all, cultural prosperity, common security, and harmony between humanity and nature.

a2444.speaker: China (government)
a2444.name: China (government)
a2444.speech: Announced an exemption from debt incurred in the form of interest-free Chinese government loans due to mature by the end of 2018, applying to Africa's least developed countries, heavily indebted and poor countries, landlocked developing countries and small island developing countries that have diplomatic relations with China.

a2444.speaker: China (at the China-Africa Internet Development and Cooperation Forum, August 2021)
a2444.name: China (at the China-Africa Internet Development and Cooperation Forum
a2444.title: August 2021)
a2444.speech: Announced its intention to formulate and implement a joint China-Africa Partnership Plan on Digital Innovation in Africa.

a2718.speaker: Balefe Sekhamane, leader of the march organizers
a2718.name: Balefe Sekhamane
a2718.title: leader of the march organizers
a2718.speech: "We were asked to go to the office of the prime minister to inquire if he would be available on the day that we are intending to hand him the letter, when we got there we were told to come back last week Thursdays for negotiations." ; said that at the negotiations at the premier's office they were told to write "a fully detailed letter and bring it back to the office", and that the response to their letter could not be guaranteed since "the office of the prime minister is very busy"; said they left the prime minister's office without reaching an agreement because they believe the office was merely trying to frustrate the planned march. ; "We presented the letter as written, but they told us to go back and submit a more detailed one. It felt like a waste of time - just a tactic to postpone the march, which was supposed to happen on June 18." ; "The officers couldn't help us or approve our request."

a2718.speaker: Balefe Sekhamane, leader of the march organizers
a2718.name: Balefe Sekhamane
a2718.title: leader of the march organizers
a2718.speech: "Since the Prime Minister's office refuses to confirm when they will respond - what if they take two years? We have advised ourselves to approach the courts." ; "The police asked us to confirm whether the prime minister's office would be present during the letter handover. It felt like we were being forced to seek their permission." ; "It's clear they are deceiving us, making us rewrite a letter with no guarantee of a timely response." ; "The march will proceed once the court intervenes." ; "We won't be silenced. If the prime minister won't listen, we will take our demands to the streets - and the courts."

a2718.speaker: Balefe Sekhamane, leader of the march organizers
a2718.name: Balefe Sekhamane
a2718.title: leader of the march organizers
a2718.speech: "First, they delay our protest. Then, they ignore our demands. It's clear they're shielding the powerful."

a2718.speaker: Protesters / march organizers (Disgruntled Basotho)
a2718.name: Protesters / march organizers (Disgruntled Basotho)
a2718.speech: claim authorities are deliberately obstructing their planned protest to the Prime Minister's office and allege these demands are unnecessary hurdles to silence dissent over LEC's mismanagement and rising costs; demand a 30 percent reduction in domestic electricity tariffs and accountability for alleged embezzlement at the LEC, with stolen funds recovered from fraudsters; allege that the prime minister's office is protecting LEC leadership rather than addressing corruption. "People are tired of corruption. If the government doesn't act, protests could escalate."

a2718.speaker: An LEC insider who requested anonymity
a2718.name: An LEC insider who requested anonymity
a2718.speech: "Money meant to maintain infrastructure and keep prices stable has been looted. Now, ordinary Basotho pay the price through higher bills and unreliable supply."

a2718.speaker: Lineo Khoarai, caller on a local radio station's phone-in morning talk show
a2718.name: Lineo Khoarai
a2718.title: caller on a local radio station's phone-in morning talk show
a2718.speech: "If there's nothing to hide, why no investigation? The longer this goes unchecked, the more it looks like a cover-up."

a2770.speaker: Ouattara Karim, Director General of Burida (Bureau ivoirien du droit d'auteur)
a2770.name: Ouattara Karim
a2770.title: Director General of Burida (Bureau ivoirien du droit d'auteur)
a2770.speech: Recalled that this remuneration is based, on the one hand, on the collection of a levy on the importation and manufacture on national territory of equipment intended for reprographic reproduction such as photocopiers, printers and scanners; and on the other hand, on the collection of a levy on reprography services (acts of reproduction) offered to the public.

a2770.speaker: Françoise Remarck, Minister of Culture and Francophonie of Côte d'Ivoire
a2770.name: Françoise Remarck
a2770.title: Minister of Culture and Francophonie of Côte d'Ivoire
a2770.speech: "We are fully aware that establishing an effective framework for remuneration for reprographic reproduction requires close collaboration between the various parties involved," she said at the opening of the workshop ; went on to add that this framework offers an ideal and relevant platform for sharing experiences, creating synergies and strengthening ties between key actors.

a2770.speaker: Françoise Remarck, Minister of Culture and Francophonie of Côte d'Ivoire
a2770.name: Françoise Remarck
a2770.title: Minister of Culture and Francophonie of Côte d'Ivoire
a2770.speech: Acknowledged that in Côte d'Ivoire the implementation of this mechanism faces some difficulties, which is why, she said, the holding of these meetings is to be welcomed.

a2770.speaker: Burida (Bureau ivoirien du droit d'auteur)
a2770.name: Burida (Bureau ivoirien du droit d'auteur)
a2770.speech: Explains that the authors of these works have, by virtue of the copyright law, exclusive rights under which any person wishing to make a copy of the said works must request and obtain their authorisation, possibly against payment of remuneration.

a2861.speaker: European Commission (statement)
a2861.name: European Commission (statement)
a2861.speech: Said in a statement on Thursday that “these funds are set to be channelled across West and Central Africa, the Sahel, the Lake Chad basin, North-West Nigeria, Central Africa, the Great Lakes region and the Greater Horn of Africa”; the statement added that the Middle East and North Africa will receive €470m, with €375m focused on the Middle East, particularly Gaza, while €95m is allocated to North Africa and Yemen

a2861.speaker: European Union (EU)
a2861.name: European Union (EU)
a2861.speech: Announced an initial humanitarian assistance package of €1.9 billion for 2025, with €510m earmarked for Nigeria and other countries in sub-Saharan Africa, and noted that the assistance will help tackle the escalating humanitarian crises expected to affect over 300 million people worldwide in 2025

a2861.speaker: Hadja Lahbib, EU Commissioner for Equality, Preparedness, and Crisis Management
a2861.name: Hadja Lahbib
a2861.title: EU Commissioner for Equality, Preparedness, and Crisis Management
a2861.speech: Emphasised the importance of ensuring safe and unimpeded access to vulnerable populations and that funding alone is insufficient without adherence to international humanitarian law. “With more than 300 million people needing humanitarian assistance in 2025, the EU is upholding its commitment to help those most in need as a leading humanitarian aid donor. Our humanitarian aid funding will support our partners on the ground – the UN family, the Red Cross/Red Crescent family, international and local government and non-governmental organisations – to provide life-saving, emergency assistance where needed”

a2884.speaker: European Union
a2884.name: European Union
a2884.speech: Two months into the war in Tigray, the European Union suspended 107 million dollars in direct budget support for Ethiopia, calling for "unfettered access to humanitarian assistance in the war-ravaged region."

a2884.speaker: Chane Shimeka, government parliamentary whip
a2884.name: Chane Shimeka
a2884.title: government parliamentary whip
a2884.speech: Development partners have "failed to keep their promises," compelling parliament to pass a bill for 26.4 billion Br in supplementary budget, according to Chane Shimeka. He admitted last month that the federal government was unable to secure finance from external sources.

a2884.speaker: Senior advisor at the Ministry of Finance (anonymous)
a2884.name: Senior advisor at the Ministry of Finance (anonymous)
a2884.speech: Fears the problem may continue in the coming fiscal year, unless the situation in the northern part of the country improves. "Ethiopia does not seem a favourite child of the west now," he told Fortune. "This may lead to further restrictions on financial support to the country, particularly from the EU and the United States."

a2884.speaker: Alemayehu Geda, professor of Economics at Addis Ababa University
a2884.name: Alemayehu Geda
a2884.title: professor of Economics at Addis Ababa University
a2884.speech: Concurs with the fear. He saw a drastic fall in grants as budgetary support to the federal government over the past two years. It was severe on forex inflow, harsher than its impact on deficit financing, according to Alemayehu.

a2884.speaker: Ahmed Shide, Minister of Finance
a2884.name: Ahmed Shide
a2884.title: Minister of Finance
a2884.speech: According to Ahmed Shide, the funds that will be used to finance public projects are already committed. "We'll face no problem during the disbursement of the finance," he told Parliament, appearing before the Revenue, Budget, & Finance Standing Committee.

a2884.speaker: Experts
a2884.name: Experts
a2884.speech: Applaud the action taken to boost the revenues of regions. But some are not pleased with the attention the agricultural sector received ; experts caution officials to be mindful of the inflationary pressure and its impact on household spending.

a2884.speaker: Demis Chanyalew (PhD), economist
a2884.name: Demis Chanyalew (PhD)
a2884.title: economist
a2884.speech: "The budget allocated to the agriculture sector is usually low. More finance to regions would help the federal government offset this."

a2884.speaker: Alemayehu Geda, professor of Economics at Addis Ababa University
a2884.name: Alemayehu Geda
a2884.title: professor of Economics at Addis Ababa University
a2884.speech: Observed that government tax revenue is growing at a slower pace than the inflation rate. "It's not growing in real terms," he told Fortune.

a2896.speaker: Sen. Oluremi Tinubu, Wife of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu / Global and National Stop TB Champion
a2896.name: Sen. Oluremi Tinubu
a2896.title: Wife of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu / Global and National Stop TB Champion
a2896.speech: Has expressed confidence in Nigeria's ability to eliminate tuberculosis (TB) by 2035, emphasizing the importance of partnerships and innovation in tackling the country's TB burden; commended stakeholders for their efforts but urged for sustained commitment to achieving global TB targets ; “Nigeria remains the country with the highest TB burden in Africa and ranks sixth globally. According to the 2024 WHO Global Tuberculosis Report, Nigeria recorded approximately 467,000 TB cases in 2023, underscoring the urgency of our collective fight against this disease,” she stated ; lauded progress in diagnosing and treating TB, attributing it to the commitment of the Federal Government under President Bola Tinubu's Renewed Hope Agenda, civil society organizations, and international partners like USAID and the Global Fund ; reaffirmed her dedication to eradicating TB, announcing that her earlier donation had been utilized to procure diagnostic tools, boosting case detection. “The solution to ending TB lies in the strength of our partnerships public and private and the integrated delivery of services that leave no one behind,” she said ; “Together, united in purpose, we can and will end TB in Nigeria,” she concluded, calling for sustained investment, innovation, and community involvement to achieve a TB-free Nigeria.

a2896.speaker: Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare
a2896.name: Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare
a2896.speech: Emphasized the urgent need for unity and collaboration in the fight against tuberculosis (TB) and highlighted the nation's commitment to leveraging health as a unifying force under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu's leadership. “Health touches every one of us,” the minister stated, urging stakeholders to see TB elimination as a collective mission ; He added that a major highlight of the conference was the innovative Private Sector TB Initiative, launched in July 2024, which has mobilized up to $25 million from private sector organizations; he underscored the importance of integrating TB control into workplace health programs and health insurance, noting the critical role of industries like banking, oil and gas, and telecommunications ; He called on governments, development partners, private sector actors, and civil society to adopt a multisectoral approach to TB control, emphasizing the importance of increasing domestic funding, fostering accountability, and learning from global best practices. “Let us seize this opportunity to reaffirm our commitment to a TB-free Nigeria,” the minister urged.

a2896.speaker: Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare
a2896.name: Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare
a2896.speech: Commended the First Lady, a global and national TB Ambassador, for her leadership in galvanizing efforts to combat TB: “Your Excellency, your dedication has inspired countless individuals and organizations,” the minister remarked, urging all stakeholders to follow her example of commitment and action.

a2896.speaker: Dr. Walter Kazadi Mulombo, World Health Organization (WHO) Country Representative, Nigeria
a2896.name: Dr. Walter Kazadi Mulombo
a2896.title: World Health Organization (WHO) Country Representative, Nigeria
a2896.speech: In his goodwill message hinted that Nigeria has made significant progress in controlling tuberculosis (TB), with a 50% reduction in TB-related deaths between 2015 and 2023; commended Nigeria's efforts, citing innovative approaches and collaboration between the Federal Ministry of Health and partners ; cautioned against complacency, highlighting persistent challenges, including a 60% funding gap in 2023, rising multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB), and socio-economic barriers to care; emphasized the need for bold and inclusive strategies, strengthened primary healthcare, next-generation diagnostics, and addressing social determinants like poverty and malnutrition ; urged stakeholders to adopt evidence-based, community-led interventions and prioritize domestic funding to transform Nigeria's TB response, and reiterated WHO's commitment to continued technical support and advocacy.

a2896.speaker: Dr. Queen Ogbuji-Ladipo, Acting Board Chair, Stop TB Partnership Nigeria
a2896.name: Dr. Queen Ogbuji-Ladipo
a2896.title: Acting Board Chair, Stop TB Partnership Nigeria
a2896.speech: In her welcome address said the Stop TB Partnership Nigeria, in collaboration with the National TB and Leprosy Control Programme (NTBLCP), has inaugurated the National TB Conference 2024 under the theme “Public-Private Partnership and Integrated Service Delivery: Panacea to End TB in Nigeria,” underscoring the importance of collaborative efforts in addressing TB and Nigeria's commitment to advancing inclusive, gender-responsive, and rights-based TB interventions ; She added that the conference has brought together stakeholders from Nigeria and abroad to discuss innovative strategies for eliminating TB, with key supporters including the Federal Ministry of Health, WHO, USAID, and other global health partners.

a2896.speaker: WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2024
a2896.name: WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2024
a2896.speech: According to the report, Nigeria recorded over 360,000 TB cases in 2023, accounting for 70% of the country's estimated TB burden, and Nigeria has achieved a 24% decline in TB incidence rates between 2015 and 2023.

a3058.speaker: Francois Vandeville, Secretary General of the Francophonie summit
a3058.name: Francois Vandeville
a3058.title: Secretary General of the Francophonie summit
a3058.speech: Announced at a press conference that of the 88 member States and governments of the International Organisation of La Francophonie (OIF), some fifty are expected to take part in the summit ; said with satisfaction that the summit, the first in 33 years in the organisation's host country, is "one of the four great international moments France is hosting this year", alongside the 80th anniversary of the D-Day landings, the Olympic Games and the reopening of the Notre-Dame de Paris cathedral.

a3058.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
a3058.name: Emmanuel Macron
a3058.title: President of France
a3058.speech: Sees in the Francophonie "a space for mediation", "a space for dialogue to settle political differences as is the case between the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda" ; "We will in fact try to make progress on this subject," he stated in an interview with the newspaper l'Union, referring to the talks planned with his Rwandan and Congolese counterparts to try to persuade them to conclude a peace agreement in eastern DRC.

a3058.speaker: International Organisation of La Francophonie (OIF)
a3058.name: International Organisation of La Francophonie (OIF)
a3058.speech: States that its missions are to "promote the French language", "peace, democracy and human rights", "support education" and "develop economic cooperation", and estimates the number of French speakers at 321 million across the five continents, the 5th most spoken language in the world ; according to the organisation, the rise to 715 million speakers by 2050 requires "significant support for the teaching of French".

a3058.speaker: Louise Mushikiwabo, Secretary General of the OIF
a3058.name: Louise Mushikiwabo
a3058.title: Secretary General of the OIF
a3058.speech: Acknowledged in an interview with AFP the organisation's "modest" influence, "which (is not in a position to) resolve the world's complicated crises, but can move things forward".

a3058.speaker: Amelia Lakrafi, French Macronist MP (Ensemble)
a3058.name: Amelia Lakrafi
a3058.title: French Macronist MP (Ensemble)
a3058.speech: Recommends "playing a driving role" in fields such as education, digital technology, artificial intelligence and the media; several French members of parliament called on Thursday for the Francophonie to evolve in the years ahead.

a3058.speaker: Oxfam (statement)
a3058.name: Oxfam (statement)
a3058.speech: Denounced "the hypocrisy" of France, which it says has cut a quarter of its official development assistance (ODA) over the past two years while "70 million French speakers are in need of emergency humanitarian aid".

a3058.speaker: Alan Anic, advocacy officer for Oxfam
a3058.name: Alan Anic
a3058.title: advocacy officer for Oxfam
a3058.speech: "The summit's motto is 'create, innovate and do business' but, to describe the Francophonie, the terms 'inequality, poverty and injustice' would have been more accurate."

a3058.speaker: OECD
a3058.name: OECD
a3058.speech: According to the OECD, France's official development assistance represented 0.5% of gross national income (GNI) in 2023, compared with 0.6% for Switzerland, 0.44% for Belgium and 0.38% for Canada.

a3079.speaker: USAID (message on its website)
a3079.name: USAID (message on its website)
a3079.speech: “On Friday, February 7, 2025, at 11:59 pm (EST) all USAID direct hire personnel will be placed on administrative leave globally, with the exception of designated personnel responsible for mission-critical functions, core leadership and specially designated programs. Essential personnel expected to continue working will be informed by Agency leadership by Thursday, February 6, at 3:00pm (EST).” ; “For USAID personnel currently posted outside the United States, the Agency, in coordination with missions and the Department of State, is currently preparing a plan, in accordance with all applicable requirements and laws, under which the Agency would arrange and pay for return travel to the United States within 30 days and provide for the termination of PSC and ISC contracts that are not determined to be essential. The Agency will consider case-by-case exceptions and return travel extensions based on personal or family hardship, mobility or safety concerns, or other reasons... Further guidance on how to request an exception will be forthcoming. Thank you for your service.”

a3298.speaker: Mesganu Arga, State Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ethiopia
a3298.name: Mesganu Arga
a3298.title: State Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ethiopia
a3298.speech: Emphasized the strategic cooperation between Ethiopia and the U.S. in terms of peace and security, noting that the relationship between the two countries should be further strengthened through economic cooperation ; emphasized the strong cooperation between Ethiopia and the U.S. in combating terrorism and advocated for this partnership to continue and be strengthened ; provided a briefing to the Deputy Assistant Secretary on the current situations in Sudan and Somalia.

a3298.speaker: Vincent D. Spera, U.S. Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for East Africa, Sudan, and South Sudan
a3298.name: Vincent D. Spera
a3298.title: U.S. Deputy Assistant Secretary of State for East Africa, Sudan, and South Sudan
a3298.speech: Acknowledged the historic nature of the relationship between Ethiopia and the U.S., emphasizing that the existing cooperation in security and development should be further reinforced ; recognized Ethiopia's key role in the region and stated that efforts would be made to enhance bilateral relations, particularly in the economic sector ; noted that the African Union and IGAD play critical roles, especially regarding the situation in Sudan.

a3299.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a3299.name: John Dramani Mahama
a3299.title: President of Ghana
a3299.speech: Has directed Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, the minister for Finance, to take urgent steps to bridge the funding gap arising out of the suspension of the USAID's international funding programme.

a3299.speaker: Felix Kwakye Ofosu, Spokesperson to the President (statement)
a3299.name: Felix Kwakye Ofosu
a3299.title: Spokesperson to the President (statement)
a3299.speech: Said President Mahama expressed concern over the gap created because of the order: "Of particular concern to the President, is the impact of the projected $78.2 million shortfall that would adversely impact such critical interventions as malaria prevention, maternal and child health, family planning, reproductive health, nutrition and the fight against HIV/AIDS under which the availability of antiretroviral drugs, testing and prevention programmes are threatened." ; added that the President had, therefore, requested that the bridging arrangements focused on the priority areas to mitigate any deleterious effects occasioned by the USAID funding disruptions.

a3487.speaker: Andrew Young, U.S. Ambassador to Burkina Faso
a3487.name: Andrew Young
a3487.title: U.S. Ambassador to Burkina Faso
a3487.speech: On the assessment of his tenure: "It was a particular honour to have spent these past years working in partnership with the people of Burkina Faso at a time when they must take up some of the greatest challenges in their history. You are building your democracy at the same time as you confront an odious enemy, the extremists. You are also seeking a better future for your people by growing your economy. The people of the United States are committed alongside you in all these efforts to contribute to your success." ; cited the CATWELL school feeding programmes, the exchange programmes (the Mandela Washington Fellowship for young African leaders/YALI, Fulbright, the International Visitors programme, youth leadership), local-language literacy teaching, and small grants such as the African Women's Entrepreneurship Programme (AWEP) and the Ambassador's Self-Help fund, saying these investments help displaced and marginalised people make profits and break the cycles of poverty and violence.

a3487.speaker: Andrew Young, U.S. Ambassador to Burkina Faso
a3487.name: Andrew Young
a3487.title: U.S. Ambassador to Burkina Faso
a3487.speech: On the second Millennium Challenge Corporation compact: said that in his first week he had the honour of announcing that Burkina Faso had obtained the rare distinction of being selected for a second MCC Compact, and that "today, we are on track to sign an agreement for the joint implementation of energy and human capital projects that should exceed 350 million dollars through a gift from the American people to the Burkinabe people" ; said that combining these investments with greater transparency and energy trade across West Africa could raise Burkina Faso's national income by several percentage points, and cited the MCC water management project at Di, which added more than 2,000 hectares of irrigated cropland.

a3487.speaker: A female official at the Di MCC water project (anonymous)
a3487.name: A female official at the Di MCC water project (anonymous)
a3487.speech: Indicated to us that thanks to the United States' insistence on supporting policies in favour of minority and women-led cooperatives, more than 30 such structures obtained secure land tenure in order to benefit from the project, which enabled hundreds of children, especially girls, to attend school, many of them through the BRIGHT school programmes still funded by the American people through the MCC.

a3487.speaker: Andrew Young, U.S. Ambassador to Burkina Faso
a3487.name: Andrew Young
a3487.title: U.S. Ambassador to Burkina Faso
a3487.speech: On counter-terrorism support: said that during his stay "we were able to triple the amount of American security assistance compared with the total assistance of the same type granted over the previous 12 years", that this partnership would continue the following year and could be larger than the 2020 assistance, that all U.S. aid is designed to train and help Burkina Faso assume its sovereign responsibilities to secure the state and the people against a destructive enemy, and that all aid rests on the view that state security forces must act in respect of the rule of law, the protection of human rights and accountability ; cited the Flintlock 2017 and 2018 special forces exercises with G5 Sahel partners, involving thousands of participants from 30 countries, adding "We must do more... I have faith in the Burkinabe people."

a3487.speaker: Andrew Young, U.S. Ambassador to Burkina Faso
a3487.name: Andrew Young
a3487.title: U.S. Ambassador to Burkina Faso
a3487.speech: On the future of bilateral relations: said the relationship is built on three major principles - helping Burkina Faso root its democracy, helping it confront extremism by consolidating a tolerant, multifunctional and peaceful state, and investing in a better future for all Burkinabe through long-term equitable development including improved health care ; noted that the United States is Burkina Faso's largest donor in the health sector, where together with other partners under-five child mortality has been cut by more than half over the past decade, that the U.S. remains alongside Burkina Faso in the fight against COVID-19 through institutions such as CORUS, and that over the past 20 years the United States has invested more than 1.4 billion dollars (849 billion FCFA) in Burkina Faso's development, including 222 million dollars (134 billion FCFA) in health assistance, preventing and treating malaria, increasing access to water and nutritious food, and fighting HIV/AIDS and neglected tropical diseases.

a3487.speaker: Andrew Young, U.S. Ambassador to Burkina Faso
a3487.name: Andrew Young
a3487.title: U.S. Ambassador to Burkina Faso
a3487.speech: On the memories he takes away: cited the responsiveness and generous spirit of Burkinabe, especially young people, during the "le civisme, c'est moi", "Je m'engage" and "engages ensemble" campaigns, which inspired thousands of hours of community service ; recounted his travels across the country and meeting a farmer near Gayeri who had lost everything, whom USAID helped improve water management, natural fertiliser and seeds, achieving yields three to four times higher than those not using the techniques shared by the United States, and who offered him a bull, which he accepted on condition that the farmer keep it for the next ten years so that he could return to Burkina Faso in a decade to reap the fruits of that partnership.

a3487.speaker: Villagers near Gayeri who took in a displaced farmer (anonymous)
a3487.name: Villagers near Gayeri who took in a displaced farmer (anonymous)
a3487.speech: They had little, but they said: "You can farm this land. It is extremely rocky and poor land, almost like the moon, but you can settle here."

a3513.speaker: Government of Zimbabwe
a3513.name: Government of Zimbabwe
a3513.speech: The government has said the US$3.6 billion Industrial Park in Beitbridge, which President Emmerson Mnangagwa commissioned in February this year, is expected to employ at least 10 000 people once fully operational.

a3513.speaker: Statement posted on the NDS1 X (Twitter) handle
a3513.name: Statement posted on the NDS1 X (Twitter) handle
a3513.speech: “The project, which was commissioned by President Emmerson Mnangagwa in February 2025, covers over 5 000 hectares in a Special Economic Zone. It is being implemented in five phases over a 12-year period” ; according to the statement, the massive industrial complex will integrate mining, coking, green power generation, and advanced smelting technology, and will produce a wide range of products including ferrochrome, coke, and stainless steel, positioning Zimbabwe as a key player in regional and global mineral value chains.

a3513.speaker: Zimbabwean government officials
a3513.name: Zimbabwean government officials
a3513.speech: Said the Beitbridge Industrial Park was another milestone in strengthening Zimbabwe–China relations and advancing Harare's vision of becoming an upper middle-income economy by 2030.

a3515.speaker: United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) reports
a3515.name: United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) reports
a3515.speech: Information received by the OHCHR reports summary executions of civilians attempting to escape the violence in El Fasher, some of them motivated by ethnic considerations; according to these reports the killings reported in El Fasher are mainly committed by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which target former combatants who have laid down their arms. Raw reports indicate that these RSF summarily executed five men who were trying to bring food into the regional capital of Darfur, under militia blockade for 18 months, accused of supporting the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF).

a3515.speaker: Volker Türk, United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights
a3515.name: Volker Türk
a3515.title: United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights
a3515.speech: Warned: “The risk of further large-scale violations and atrocities, motivated by ethnic considerations, in El Fasher is increasing day by day,” adding that urgent and concrete measures are needed to ensure the protection of civilians in El Fasher and the safety of those trying to leave the country.

a3515.speaker: Volker Türk, United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights
a3515.name: Volker Türk
a3515.title: United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights
a3515.speech: Urged RSF commanders to respect their obligation under international law to protect civilians and to secure the passage of humanitarian aid.

a3515.speaker: António Guterres, Secretary-General of the United Nations
a3515.name: António Guterres
a3515.title: Secretary-General of the United Nations
a3515.speech: Told journalists that this “terrible escalation” required the international community to put pressure on the countries taking sides in Sudan's internal conflict by “supplying weapons” to one of the warring parties, urging them to conclude a ceasefire.

a3515.speaker: Denise Brown, United Nations Humanitarian Coordinator for Sudan
a3515.name: Denise Brown
a3515.title: United Nations Humanitarian Coordinator for Sudan
a3515.speech: Said Monday at a press conference that civilians, adults and children, fleeing El Fasher often appear “dehydrated, poorly nourished, some wounded and all traumatised.”

a3515.speaker: Denise Brown, United Nations Humanitarian Coordinator for Sudan
a3515.name: Denise Brown
a3515.title: United Nations Humanitarian Coordinator for Sudan
a3515.speech: Said that volunteers had reportedly been killed in El Fasher, adding: “These people are the backbone of the humanitarian response in the most difficult areas and are also protected by international humanitarian law.”

a3515.speaker: United Nations
a3515.name: United Nations
a3515.speech: According to the UN, some 130 humanitarian workers have been killed since the start of the conflict more than two years ago.

a3721.speaker: House of Lords
a3721.name: House of Lords
a3721.speech: Said the UK had missed the boat and had to play catch-up in the race for Africa’s critical minerals; urged the British government to treat Africa as a place of opportunity to make money.

a3721.speaker: 2020 report, “The UK and Sub-Saharan Africa: prosperity, peace and development cooperation”
a3721.name: 2020 report
a3721.title: “The UK and Sub-Saharan Africa: prosperity, peace and development cooperation”
a3721.speech: Said several British governments had said that trade with Africa should get greater priority, but had “failed to make this a reality in the face of competing demands.”

a3721.speaker: Lord Popat of Harrow, former trade envoy to Uganda, the DRC and Rwanda
a3721.name: Lord Popat of Harrow
a3721.title: former trade envoy to Uganda, the DRC and Rwanda
a3721.speech: “We need to see Africa not as a charity, but as a place of opportunity. Politicians and diplomats believe in soft power and diplomacy... Coming from a business background, I believe in hard cash.” ; added that UK exports to Africa had dwindled: “Our exports to Africa were more than 30% not long ago. Today, they are less than 3%.” ; urged the UK to join the race for critical minerals in Africa, such as lithium: “We need access to foreign markets, particularly in Africa. Several car manufacturers have already left the UK due to significant challenges in sourcing batteries, which are critical to electric vehicle production. The uncertainty in supply chains has made the UK less competitive. The shortage of essential materials, such as cobalt, much of which come from the DRC, has further strained the UK’s car manufacturers. If we do not secure reliable supply chains for these materials, we will see a further exodus in the car industry.” ; said the UK had missed the boat: “Other nations, such as China, India, the US, and the EU, have already signed deals with the DRC, while we are still working on a memorandum of understanding. We must expedite this process. I urge the minister to look into this as a matter of urgency.” ; took credit for Arsenal’s Visit Rwanda deal, worth £30 million a year, which he said had allowed the Rwandan government to double the country’s tourism.

a3721.speaker: Lord Bruce of Bennachie
a3721.name: Lord Bruce of Bennachie
a3721.speech: Noted that relations with Africa had been constrained, even through aid cuts, and said the UK should not separate trade and aid because both speak to Africa: “I will link with the fact that aid has been drastically cut. I appreciate that we are focusing on trade, but the two are linked because the relationships grow together. The cut in aid has had a very disruptive effect on our relationships with Africa. I am glad the previous government started to restore the balance, and I hope the new government will follow that through and help us to cement new relationships.”

a3721.speaker: Lord Risby, former trade envoy to Algeria
a3721.name: Lord Risby
a3721.title: former trade envoy to Algeria
a3721.speech: Urged the British government to deploy more trade-focused envoys and allocate more funds to embassies across Africa to catch up with their counterparts from Europe: “The number of individuals devoted to trade promotion in our embassies and the budget allocated is frankly anaemic compared to that of our competitors.”

a3721.speaker: Lord Swire
a3721.name: Lord Swire
a3721.speech: Suggested that a starting point for a reset of relations with Africa could start with the Commonwealth because it “presents a real opportunity and an open market for British businesses.”

a3797.speaker: Valentin Djenontin, Minister of Justice of Benin
a3797.name: Valentin Djenontin
a3797.title: Minister of Justice of Benin
a3797.speech: After showing that corruption and cross-border crime constitute an important subject, emphasized the need to fight these scourges, which according to the minister affect "the survival of States and the security of populations."

a3797.speaker: Michael Raynor, Ambassador of the United States to Benin
a3797.name: Michael Raynor
a3797.title: Ambassador of the United States to Benin
a3797.speech: Recalling that corruption is an "old phenomenon" which causes enormous losses for the world (5% of Gross Domestic Product), noted that "the fight against corruption is nothing other than the fight for justice", and that this fight can make it possible to quadruple the revenues of countries and, for Benin, to restore its eligibility for the second compact of the Millennium Challenge Account (MCA).

a3797.speaker: President of the ANLC (National Anti-Corruption Authority of Benin)
a3797.name: President of the ANLC (National Anti-Corruption Authority of Benin)
a3797.speech: Specified in his welcome address that the "Ayifa" project aims to make the state anti-corruption structure that he chairs function.

a4135.speaker: Hakainde Hichilema, President of Zambia
a4135.name: Hakainde Hichilema
a4135.title: President of Zambia
a4135.speech: Has tipped private sector firms to deliver the best products on the local market, saying such may open the window for imports from Zambia. He said this at the second Public Private Dialogue Forum (PPDF) Private Sector Day in Lusaka.

a4416.speaker: Hamidou Sawadogo, professor of monetary and financial economics at the University Joseph KI-Zerbo
a4416.name: Hamidou Sawadogo
a4416.title: professor of monetary and financial economics at the University Joseph KI-Zerbo
a4416.speech: “This model is based on leveraging internal resources. It has enabled the head of state and his government to prioritise agriculture. But the other key aspect is the industrialisation of our production.”

a4416.speaker: Hamidou Sawadogo, professor of monetary and financial economics at the University Joseph KI-Zerbo
a4416.name: Hamidou Sawadogo
a4416.title: professor of monetary and financial economics at the University Joseph KI-Zerbo
a4416.speech: “Personally, I would recommend further investment in territorial defence to ensure our survival. Once that is secured, we can continue developing our internal growth model.”

a4606.speaker: “What We Know About Exit – Practical Guidance For Developing Exit Strategies in the Field”, a publication of the C-SAFE Regional Learning Spaces Initiative by Alison Gardner, Kara Greenblott and Erika Joubert
a4606.name: “What We Know About Exit – Practical Guidance For Developing Exit Strategies in the Field”
a4606.title: a publication of the C-SAFE Regional Learning Spaces Initiative by Alison Gardner, Kara Greenblott and Erika Joubert
a4606.speech: Cited as the source of the definitions and guidance set out: that a program “exit” refers to the withdrawal of all externally provided program resources from an entire program area; that a program Exit Strategy is a plan describing how the program intends to withdraw its resources while ensuring that achievement of the program goals is not jeopardized; and that there are three basic approaches to Exit Strategies – phasing down, phasing out and phasing over – as well as three categories of exit criteria (time limit, achievement of program impacts, and achievement of benchmarks).

a4606.speaker: C-SAFE Regional Learning Spaces Initiative (CARE, World Vision, CRS, ADRA and USAID)
a4606.name: C-SAFE Regional Learning Spaces Initiative (CARE
a4606.title: World Vision, CRS, ADRA and USAID)
a4606.speech: Identified in a footnote as the initiative behind the publication: “The C-SAFE Regional Learning Spaces is an Initiative by CARE, World Vision, CRS, ADRA and USAID.”

a4643.speaker: Dahabo, 47, resident of rural Lower Juba
a4643.name: Dahabo
a4643.title: 47, resident of rural Lower Juba
a4643.speech: "My son was at school playing with other children when a nail pierced through his shoe. His leg swelled up to the knee. I haven't slept for four nights as I was massaging and applying compresses to his leg, sometimes buying painkillers from town. Eventually, I took him to hospital for a tetanus shot. When I got there, there was nothing." ; "I don't have money to buy medicine and there is no medicine here at the health centre. I asked for my bronchitis medication but they told me it's out of stock."

a4643.speaker: Abdullahi Mohamed Isman, head of Kudhaa health centre
a4643.name: Abdullahi Mohamed Isman
a4643.title: head of Kudhaa health centre
a4643.speech: Said the facility was open but unable to deliver many services at all. "This mirrors what many rural people are going through. The good hope and morale of the people has been cut but people keep coming to the place where they used to get medicine. There are severe illnesses spreading around here such as flu, slightly less severe than Corona virus but heavier than the usual flu. People are suffering greatly from that flu. There is also acute watery diarrhoea affecting adults and children. Among our neighbours, there is a lot of trouble with serious skin conditions that many people are suffering from. These diseases are spreading at a time when health centres have no medicine or funds."

a4643.speaker: Bashir Said Diriye, father of eight living in Kulbiyow
a4643.name: Bashir Said Diriye
a4643.title: father of eight living in Kulbiyow
a4643.speech: Said he was forced to take his four children across the border to Haluqo in neighbouring Kenya after they contracted malaria, and that the trip cost him $112, which he borrowed because he could not bear to see his children suffer. "The children all got malaria and were malnourished. They wasted away and became weak. There was no proper medicine available where I lived. Later, I took them to Haluqo and had them treated there in the middle of last month. Now the children are not suffering, they are well." ; Said he fears new illnesses may arise from contaminated water and rising mosquito activity in his area after the rain ; On his income from a meat stall at the Kulbiyow slaughterhouse: "That's where I get money for the children's expenses, but sometimes we earn and sometimes we don't it varies."

a4643.speaker: Local people in Lower Juba, including those interviewed for the report
a4643.name: Local people in Lower Juba
a4643.title: including those interviewed for the report
a4643.speech: Hope that the Federal Government of Somalia and the Jubbaland administration will step in to support their healthcare services.

a4843.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (as a candidate)
a4843.name: Donald Trump
a4843.title: US President (as a candidate)
a4843.speech: Said he didn't even plan to read Project 2025, much less endorse it.

a4843.speaker: Heritage Foundation / Project 2025 (922-page governing blueprint)
a4843.name: Heritage Foundation / Project 2025 (922-page governing blueprint)
a4843.speech: Recommended reclassifying federal workers to make them easier to fire, and stripping protections from civil servants perceived as disloyal ; reinforced Trump's conspiracy theory about a "deep state" working to undermine Republicans as it called for an end to the "weaponisation" of government ; demanded that intelligence chiefs undo the "damage" done by investigations into the Trump campaign and its coordination with Russia's attack on the 2016 US election ; was also an early proponent of Trump's hiring freeze for career officials.

a4843.speaker: Heritage Foundation / Project 2025 (922-page governing blueprint)
a4843.name: Heritage Foundation / Project 2025 (922-page governing blueprint)
a4843.speech: Called for the reinstatement of military personnel discharged for refusing Covid-19 vaccines, and said transgender troops should be kicked out ; called for an end to "Marxist indoctrination" in the military, singling out diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) initiatives in the armed forces and across the government ; recommended purging the federal bureaucracy of terms considered "woke" by conservatives, from "sexual orientation" and "gender identity" to "reproductive rights" ; said "Sex" should mean biological sex recognised at birth and has nothing to do with people's identity preferences ; recommended revoking the Biden administration memorandum supporting abortion access abroad.

a4843.speaker: Heritage Foundation / Project 2025 (922-page governing blueprint)
a4843.name: Heritage Foundation / Project 2025 (922-page governing blueprint)
a4843.speech: In education, pushed for parental choice and wanted the Civil Rights Act (CRA) invoked to end "gender ideology and critical race theory" in schools.

a4843.speaker: Heritage Foundation / Project 2025 (922-page governing blueprint)
a4843.name: Heritage Foundation / Project 2025 (922-page governing blueprint)
a4843.speech: Wanted state and local police to be involved in immigration raids and pushed for the mandatory detention of undocumented migrants ; said countries that don't take back deported citizens should face "stiff sanctions".

a4843.speaker: Heritage Foundation / Project 2025 (922-page governing blueprint)
a4843.name: Heritage Foundation / Project 2025 (922-page governing blueprint)
a4843.speech: Called specifically for drilling in Alaska ; called for the abolition of renewable energy subsidies and efficiency requirements for household appliances.

a4843.speaker: Heritage Foundation / Project 2025 (922-page governing blueprint)
a4843.name: Heritage Foundation / Project 2025 (922-page governing blueprint)
a4843.speech: "US foreign aid is too often disconnected from the strategy and practice of US foreign policy," Project 2025 said ; had foreshadowed the president's tariffs crackdown and pushed for his withdrawal from the World Health Organisation.

a4843.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4843.name: Donald Trump
a4843.title: US President
a4843.speech: Said it was US policy to "fully avail itself of Alaska's vast lands and resources".

a4843.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4843.name: Donald Trump
a4843.title: US President
a4843.speech: Halted all foreign aid in his first week back in office, saying the system was "not aligned with American interests".

a4843.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4843.name: Donald Trump
a4843.title: US President
a4843.speech: Ordered an end to hiring practices based on "illegal racial discrimination under the guise of 'equity'" and set US policy to recognise "two sexes, male and female" ; declared gender dysphoria inconsistent with troop "readiness" and "lethality".

a4843.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4843.name: Donald Trump
a4843.title: US President
a4843.speech: Directed officials to ensure that diplomacy includes "the foreign states' acceptance of their nationals who are subject to removal from the United States" ; announced the creation of new "federal-state partnerships" on immigration enforcement.

a4843.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4843.name: Donald Trump
a4843.title: US President
a4843.speech: Issued edicts prioritising "education freedom" and cited the Civil Rights Act in an executive order withdrawing funding from public schools failing to respect parents' rights and discrimination laws.

a4876.speaker: United Nations
a4876.name: United Nations
a4876.speech: The United Nations denounces collective sexual violations in Sudan, following the civil war in the country.

a4876.speaker: United Nations report / UN fact-finding mission (report)
a4876.name: United Nations report / UN fact-finding mission (report)
a4876.speech: A report by the Organization says that the violence has been used as a means of terrorising and punishing civilians ; the mission concluded that the Sudanese army and the Rapid Support Forces committed large-scale violations of human rights and international humanitarian law, many of which may constitute war crimes and/or crimes against humanity.

a4876.speaker: Mohamed Chande Othman, President of a United Nations fact-finding mission
a4876.name: Mohamed Chande Othman
a4876.title: President of a United Nations fact-finding mission
a4876.speech: Revealed on Tuesday that the escalation of sexual violence committed in Sudan is staggering, in a context in which the country has been at war since April 2023 between the Sudanese army (SAF), under the command of the country's de facto ruler Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), led by his former vice-president Mohamed Hamdan Daglo ; accuses the paramilitaries in particular of committing such acts.

a4965.speaker: Antônio Supeia, Secretary of State in Cabo Delgado province
a4965.name: Antônio Supeia
a4965.title: Secretary of State in Cabo Delgado province
a4965.speech: Said that he expected twin gains from the action taken; firstly, the economic empowerment of producers, through the sale of surplus sesame, and second, the reinforcement of food self-sufficiency through the production of corn and nhemba bean ; said the objective of this project was not only to grant humanitarian assistance, but also to assist sustainable and integrated development, aiming at the rapid recovery of affected families through agricultural production, consequently improving the general quality of life of the population.

a5127.speaker: Kenedid Ibrahim Houssein, President of the Union of the Francophone Press of Djibouti (UPF-Djibouti)
a5127.name: Kenedid Ibrahim Houssein
a5127.title: President of the Union of the Francophone Press of Djibouti (UPF-Djibouti)
a5127.speech: Recalled the important role played by the national media in the fight against COVID-19 and in the promotion and protection of children's rights: “The national press has a paramount role to play in defending children's rights and is committed to working alongside UNICEF to advance the cause of children.”

a5127.speaker: Melva Johnson, UNICEF Representative in Djibouti
a5127.name: Melva Johnson
a5127.title: UNICEF Representative in Djibouti
a5127.speech: Welcomed the collaboration between UNICEF and UPF-Djibouti aimed at involving media professionals in the promotion and protection of children's rights: “The Republic of Djibouti has made great efforts to improve the conditions of children with the support of its partners such as UNICEF.” ; Stressed the importance of the media and journalists in promoting children's rights, and particularly their crucial role in the context marked by COVID-19 in providing accurate and reliable information to the public; congratulated the laureates of this first edition of the prize for their commitment and professionalism and encouraged journalists to continue their work in favour of children's rights.

a5127.speaker: Aicha Mohamed Robleh, technical adviser to the Minister of Communication in charge of Posts and Telecommunications
a5127.name: Aicha Mohamed Robleh
a5127.title: technical adviser to the Minister of Communication in charge of Posts and Telecommunications
a5127.speech: Recalled that the media play an important role in the promotion and protection of children's rights, and that the prize is an opportunity to involve them further in protecting these small vulnerable beings: “The media have a considerable impact on the way we see the world and are therefore very well placed to influence our attitudes towards children's rights. In the course of their work, they can prompt governments, the public and civil society to make changes. They can both raise debates on children's problems and give children the means to express their own opinions.”

a5402.speaker: Presidency of the Republic of Mozambique (statement)
a5402.name: Presidency of the Republic of Mozambique (statement)
a5402.speech: Said Daniel Chapo's visit will run until 30 October and aims "to strengthen the relations of friendship, solidarity and cooperation between the two countries," and that he will be accompanied by three ministers and two secretaries of state ; added that during the stay the Head of State will meet with Vice-President JD Vance "to exchange impressions on deepening the dialogue between the two countries and peoples, as well as strengthening bilateral relations," and will hold meetings "with other US official entities and financial and development institutions," with the agenda including participation in "business roundtables" in Washington and Houston, Texas, as well as a "fundraising gala for conservation actions."

a5402.speaker: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a5402.name: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a5402.speech: Announced about a month earlier the decision to continue the previously announced programme of US$500 million (about EUR 422.2 million), to be financed in Mozambique, for connectivity and coastal resilience, following a review process.

a5402.speaker: US Embassy in Maputo (statement released 18 September)
a5402.name: US Embassy in Maputo (statement released 18 September)
a5402.speech: Said that following the External Assistance Review, the MCC board of directors met in August "and recommended advancing the Mozambique Coastal Connectivity and Resilience Compact" ; "This recommendation reflects continued confidence in the cooperation between the US and Mozambique, highlighting the commitment to generate tangible results for both peoples," adding that the programme "is fully aligned with US foreign policy priorities" and "aims to produce concrete benefits" for both peoples.

a5402.speaker: Lusa (news agency)
a5402.name: Lusa (news agency)
a5402.speech: Reported last December an announcement that MCC-Mozambique had planned to launch at the beginning of this year the tender for the construction of the new bridge over the Licungo River and a ring road, which did not then take place.

a5664.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a5664.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a5664.speech: Is now recommending that countries include an HIV drug newly approved for prevention, lenacapavir, as a tool in their efforts to fight HIV infections – especially for groups most at risk and in areas where the burden of HIV remains high; the global recommendation was issued Monday at the International AIDS Conference in Kigali, Rwanda. According to WHO, about 40 million people globally were living with HIV at the end of 2023.

a5664.speaker: Dr. Meg Doherty, director of WHO's Department of Global HIV, Hepatitis and Sexually Transmitted Infections Programmes
a5664.name: Dr. Meg Doherty
a5664.title: director of WHO's Department of Global HIV, Hepatitis and Sexually Transmitted Infections Programmes
a5664.speech: “These new recommendations are designed for real-world use. WHO is working closely with countries and partners to support the implementation” ; “The first recommendation is that a long-acting injectable, lenacapavir, should be offered as an additional prevention choice for people at risk for HIV and as part of combination prevention. With that, we call it a strong recommendation with moderate to high certainty of the evidence” ; “LEN is a six-monthly injectable option, and it may be particularly attractive for people who prefer fewer clinic visits or have challenges with daily oral PrEP. … It could improve adherence and reach more people who need HIV prevention and can be used in pregnant and breastfeeding women” ; “WHO is providing technical assistance to countries interested in adopting LEN and simplified testing strategies, in coordination with global partners like the Global Fund, UNAIDS and several other partners and donors” ; “We call on governments, funders, implementers and civil society to work together for implementing and integrating LEN into the HIV programs. And we believe time to act is now.”

a5664.speaker: United Nations
a5664.name: United Nations
a5664.speech: International assistance accounts for 80% of prevention programs in low- and middle-income countries, according to the United Nations.

a5664.speaker: Gilead Sciences
a5664.name: Gilead Sciences
a5664.speech: Announced Wednesday that it has reached an agreement with the nonprofit Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria to supply lenacapavir for HIV prevention at no profit to the company; the company added that the cost of lenacapavir under this agreement remains confidential, and that the US annual list price of $28,218 for prevention is similar to the price of other prevention medicine options.

a5664.speaker: Daniel O'Day, Gilead Chairman and CEO
a5664.name: Daniel O'Day
a5664.title: Gilead Chairman and CEO
a5664.speech: “We are providing the medicine at no profit to Gilead, and in enough supply to reach up to two million people in low- and lower-middle-income countries ahead of generic lenacapavir becoming available.”

a5664.speaker: Peter Sands, executive director of the Global Fund
a5664.name: Peter Sands
a5664.title: executive director of the Global Fund
a5664.speech: Said lenacapavir can “fundamentally change the trajectory of the HIV epidemic,” but only if it reaches the people who need it most ; “Our ambition is to reach 2 million people with long-acting PrEP. But we can only do that if the world steps up with the resources required” ; “This is a pivotal moment — not just for the fight against HIV, but for the fundamental principle that lifesaving innovations must reach those who need them most — whoever they are, and wherever they live.”

a5664.speaker: United Nations report released Thursday
a5664.name: United Nations report released Thursday
a5664.speech: Warned that millions more people could die from HIV-related causes by 2029 if funding for HIV programs permanently disappears; among the 60 low- and middle-income countries included in the report, 25 have indicated increasing their domestic budgets for HIV response efforts next year, but the report noted that may not be sufficient to replace the scale of international funding that these countries have been heavily reliant on.

a5664.speaker: Mary Mahy, director of UNAIDS's Data for Impact department
a5664.name: Mary Mahy
a5664.title: director of UNAIDS's Data for Impact department
a5664.speech: “We know that PEPFAR had committed $4.3 billion to over 50 countries in 2025, and that support was suddenly ended in January of 2025” ; “If none of the PEPFAR funding is replaced, we'd expect something like 4 million additional deaths between 2025 and 2029, and another 6 million additional new infections” ; “We also know that drug resistance would likely occur with some of those people going off treatment.” According to Mahy, some countries already have seen effects of the rollback of funding for HIV programs.

a5664.speaker: UNAIDS data
a5664.name: UNAIDS data
a5664.speech: In Nigeria, facilities reported about 40,000 people who received PrEP at least once during the later part of last year, a number that dropped to fewer than 7,000 in April; in Kenya, about 3,000 women already received medications and nearly 900 initiated medications in October 2024, but those numbers fell to only about 300 already receiving and 100 starting medications in April.

a5664.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, UNAIDS Executive Director
a5664.name: Winnie Byanyima
a5664.title: UNAIDS Executive Director
a5664.speech: “This is not just a funding gap — it's a ticking time bomb. … We have seen services vanish overnight. Health workers have been sent home. And people — especially children and key populations — are being pushed out of care” ; “There is still time to transform this crisis into an opportunity” ; “Countries are stepping up with domestic funding.
