Communities are showing what works. We now need global solidarity to match their courage and resilience.”

a5806.speaker: One viewer (Facebook post)
a5806.name: One viewer (Facebook post)
a5806.speech: “Kabambe is on another level altogether. His mastery of economics and clear vision for Malawi show that he is prepared to lead with both clarity and strategy.”

a5806.speaker: Another viewer (on Joyce Banda's performance)
a5806.name: Another viewer (on Joyce Banda's performance)
a5806.speech: “We cannot continue to live a life of dependency, begging for support 65 years after independence. This same mindset contributed to her being voted out during her tenure. There is no solid economic blueprint in her argument.”

a5806.speaker: Another citizen (on Atupele Muluzi's performance)
a5806.name: Another citizen (on Atupele Muluzi's performance)
a5806.speech: “I honestly find nothing tangible in his responses. He often seems unsure, even as other candidates explain their policies with confidence.”

a5806.speaker: Another citizen (on Malawi's domestic resources)
a5806.name: Another citizen (on Malawi's domestic resources)
a5806.speech: “Malawi has money. What we need are leaders who know how to harness our resources and transform the economy.”

a5806.speaker: Malawi Revenue Authority (MRA) (reported figures)
a5806.name: Malawi Revenue Authority (MRA) (reported figures)
a5806.speech: reported collection of K4 to K5 trillion annually.

a5806.speaker: Institute for Public Opinion Research (IPOR) (study)
a5806.name: Institute for Public Opinion Research (IPOR) (study)
a5806.speech: A recent study shows that Malawians value and support the need for the presidential debates.

a6165.speaker: State Department official (unnamed)
a6165.name: State Department official (unnamed)
a6165.speech: Said 1107 members of the civil service and 246 Foreign Service diplomatic employees were terminated.

a6165.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6165.name: Donald Trump
a6165.title: US President
a6165.speech: Says he wants to dismantle what he calls the “deep state.”

a6165.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a6165.name: Marco Rubio
a6165.title: US Secretary of State
a6165.speech: Says the foreign policy department is too cumbersome and requires thinning out of some 15 percent.

a6165.speaker: American Foreign Service Association (AFSA), union representing State Department employees (statement)
a6165.name: American Foreign Service Association (AFSA)
a6165.title: union representing State Department employees (statement)
a6165.speech: Condemned the “catastrophic blow to our national interests”: “At a moment of great global instability — with war raging in Ukraine, conflict between Israel and Iran, and authoritarian regimes testing the boundaries of international order — the United States has chosen to gut its frontline diplomatic workforce” ; “We oppose this decision in the strongest terms.”

a6165.speaker: State Department fact sheet
a6165.name: State Department fact sheet
a6165.speech: According to a fact sheet, the State Department employed over 80,000 people worldwide last year, with around 17,700 in domestic roles.

a6165.speaker: The Washington Post
a6165.name: The Washington Post
a6165.speech: According to The Washington Post, State Department employees were informed of their firings by email; Foreign Service officers will lose their jobs 120 days after receiving the notice and will be immediately placed on administrative leave, while civil service employees will be separated after 60 days.

a6165.speaker: Ned Price, former State Department spokesman under Joe Biden
a6165.name: Ned Price
a6165.title: former State Department spokesman under Joe Biden
a6165.speech: Condemned what he called haphazard firings, saying on X: “For all the talk about ‘merit-based,’ they’re firing officers based on where they happen to be assigned on this arbitrary day” ; “It’s the laziest, most inefficient, and most damaging way to lean the workforce.”

a6165.speaker: Barbara Leaf, former ambassador and Biden’s top Middle East diplomat
a6165.name: Barbara Leaf
a6165.title: former ambassador and Biden’s top Middle East diplomat
a6165.speech: Said the move “will have terrible consequences for our ability to protect American citizens abroad, pursue and defend the national interest and our national security” ; “This is not a re-org. This is a purge,” Leaf said in a post on LinkedIn.

a6238.speaker: Rede Viária de Moçambique (REVIMO)
a6238.name: Rede Viária de Moçambique (REVIMO)
a6238.speech: Explained that four tollgates, not three, will be suspended in Gaza province because the tariffs charged do not make them sustainable, and that the unsustainability has caused the concessionaire to accumulate losses.

a6238.speaker: Sérgio Nhancale, REVIMO spokesperson
a6238.name: Sérgio Nhancale
a6238.title: REVIMO spokesperson
a6238.speech: Said in an interview that there had been an expectation of improvements in the flow of vehicles at the tollgates after the rehabilitation of the roads, which should consequently have boosted the economy, but that this did not happen: “What happens is that these investments that were in the Government's portfolio ended up not being carried out. The projections included traffic growth, which is the primary element for the viability of the business. Therefore, what was projected did not happen.” ; “We recognise four classes of vehicles... for class 1 vehicles the model foresaw a charge of 150 meticais, however the approved rate was 50 meticais... for class 4, which is for heavy vehicles, the model foresaw 1,125 but the approved rate was 1,000 meticais.”

a6238.speaker: Sérgio Nhancale, REVIMO spokesperson
a6238.name: Sérgio Nhancale
a6238.title: REVIMO spokesperson
a6238.speech: On the amount lost with the construction of the tollgates and rehabilitation of the roads, explained: “There is work that is going to be done, that will work on the implementation, looking at Revimo's situation, at the operation of these roads, and discuss the compensation mechanisms. The suspension rests on the idea that the stretches are not viable and the Government will in principle take over the operation of these infrastructures.”

a6238.speaker: Sérgio Nhancale, REVIMO spokesperson
a6238.name: Sérgio Nhancale
a6238.title: REVIMO spokesperson
a6238.speech: On the tollgates destroyed during the post-election protests in Maputo, says that those of Cumbeza and Mahubo remain inoperative, and that they are expected to operate again next July.

a6375.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana (address to the 80th UN General Assembly)
a6375.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6375.title: President of Ghana (address to the 80th UN General Assembly)
a6375.speech: Began by confronting the stark realities of a world at a crossroads, where rising nationalism, economic instability, and a breakdown in multilateralism threaten global peace; painted a vivid contrast between the world of 1945 and today's era of digital connectivity, climate crises, and geopolitical tensions; underscored the urgency of addressing climate change, a crisis disproportionately impacting the Global South despite its lower contribution to greenhouse gas emissions.

a6375.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6375.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6375.title: President of Ghana
a6375.speech: Challenged the outdated structures of global governance, particularly the UN Security Council, where Africa remains excluded from permanent representation despite its 54 member states; echoed Nelson Mandela's 1995 call for reform, demanding at least one permanent African seat with veto power and a mechanism to challenge the absolute veto held by the five permanent members; argued that the UN's founding principle of "sovereign equality" is undermined when a single nation can wield unchecked power to serve its own interests.

a6375.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6375.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6375.title: President of Ghana
a6375.speech: Called for a reset of the global financial architecture, which he described as rigged against Africa; highlighted inequities in institutions like the IMF and World Bank, advocating for greater African influence in multilateral financial systems; urged the lifting of the blockade on Cuba, citing its historical solidarity with Africa in the fight against apartheid; and emphasized the UN's role as the "proverbial town square" where nations must unite to address global challenges.

a6375.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6375.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6375.title: President of Ghana
a6375.speech: Spoke candidly about the humanitarian crises in Gaza and Sudan; rejected euphemisms, calling for a halt to the "crimes" in Gaza and supporting a two-state solution for Palestine, not as a reward for violence but as justice for innocent civilians facing collective punishment; in Sudan, drew attention to the world's largest humanitarian crisis, with 12 million displaced, urging the global community to extend the same compassion to these refugees as it did to those from Ukraine.

a6375.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6375.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6375.title: President of Ghana
a6375.speech: Declared: "The future is African." With projections that Africa will account for over 25% of the world's population and one-third of its youth by 2050, he positioned the continent as a catalyst for human potential, economic reform, and ecological stability; rejecting centuries-old lenses of racism, colonialism, and implicit bias, he celebrated Africa's resilience and its capacity to redefine global narratives.

a6375.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6375.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6375.title: President of Ghana
a6375.speech: Called for an end to the era of foreign exploitation of Africa's natural wealth, advocating for fairer negotiations to ensure the continent retains a greater share of its resources, which he argued is essential to fund the well-being of African citizens and break the cycle of poverty-stricken communities living on the margins of foreign-controlled concessions.

a6375.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, African Union Champion for Financial Institutions and Reparations
a6375.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6375.title: African Union Champion for Financial Institutions and Reparations
a6375.speech: Made a historic demand for the recognition of the slave trade as the greatest crime against humanity; announced Ghana's intent to introduce a motion at the UNGA for reparations, encompassing financial redress, the return of looted cultural artifacts, and acknowledgment of the wealth created for Western nations through the enslavement and colonization of Africans; highlighted the hypocrisy of historical reparations paid to slave owners for their "lost property" while the descendants of the enslaved continue to seek justice.

a6375.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6375.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6375.title: President of Ghana
a6375.speech: Addressed the steep cuts in Official Development Assistance, noting a 40% drop in humanitarian aid to Africa since July 2024; urged African nations to leverage their resources to achieve self-reliance, reducing dependency on external aid and fostering dignity through economic empowerment.

a6375.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6375.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6375.title: President of Ghana
a6375.speech: Showcased Ghana's ongoing "reset agenda" as a blueprint for progress, noting that in just eight months his administration reduced inflation from 23.8% in December 2024 to 11.5% in August 2025, stabilized the Ghana cedi, and improved the country's sovereign credit rating; emphasized the 24-Hour Economy Initiative, lean governance, anti-corruption measures, and trust-building with citizens as key drivers of the turnaround; highlighted Ghana's commitment to gender equality, celebrating the election of Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang as the country's first female Vice President.

a6375.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6375.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6375.title: President of Ghana
a6375.speech: Warned against the dangers of digital isolation, where algorithms reinforce division and disinformation, undermining the connectivity promised by technology; in an era of rising xenophobia and nationalism, celebrated the contributions of African migrants and their descendants, citing figures like Maame Ewusi-Mensah Frimpong, the first Black female judge on California's federal district courts, and Peter Bossman, the first Black mayor in Slovenia's history.

a6375.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a6375.name: John Dramani Mahama
a6375.title: President of Ghana
a6375.speech: In closing, reaffirmed the UN's vital role as the world's gathering place, urging its preservation amid global fragmentation; congratulated the Assembly's President on her historic election as the fifth woman in the role and expressed hope for a future female UN Secretary-General; for Africa, for Ghana, and for his 18-year-old daughter, envisioned a world of safety, equality, and opportunity.

a6557.speaker: Self Help Africa
a6557.name: Self Help Africa
a6557.speech: Says that the Programme of Activities (PoA) aims to support local organisations and companies to participate in the Carbon Market which will help tackle financial challenges, reduce carbon emissions, conserve the environment, and promote health and economic development towards Malawians.

a6557.speaker: Charles Matewere, Self Help Africa Project Manager
a6557.name: Charles Matewere
a6557.title: Self Help Africa Project Manager
a6557.speech: Said engaging stakeholders meaningfully is important in enhancing project design and outcomes. Matewere explained that the consultation aims to inform stakeholders about the project, discuss its potential positive and negative impacts, and establish a continuous engagement process for stakeholders to provide input and raise concerns throughout the project's lifecycle. He noted that the Programme of Activities allows for the registration of multiple similar carbon projects as a single programme, reducing transaction costs and increasing management efficiency ; "We are establishing a Programme of Activities and need to consult various stakeholders to gather their views, which will be essential for our registration process. We want to hear the thoughts and expectations of those involved in this initiative."

a6557.speaker: Charles Matewere, Self Help Africa Project Manager
a6557.name: Charles Matewere
a6557.title: Self Help Africa Project Manager
a6557.speech: Added that participating in the carbon market presents huge financial opportunities. He mentioned the need to support people and projects aimed at mitigating carbon emissions, noting that current participation levels are low ; "Self Help Africa is committed to opening doors for those lacking financial and technical capacity."

a6557.speaker: Benson Chidaomba, Lilongwe City Council's Environment Health Officer
a6557.name: Benson Chidaomba
a6557.title: Lilongwe City Council's Environment Health Officer
a6557.speech: Welcomed the Programme of Activities citing the council's responsibility to address environmental and health issues in the community ; "It is crucial to consider projects like this, especially since health concerns are often overlooked. Cooking activities produce harmful emissions, such as carbon dioxide from the smoke, which can lead to health issues like tuberculosis. The Lilongwe City Council will play a role in disseminating information to improve community health during the project's implementation."

a6595.speaker: Christine N. Umutoni, UN Resident Coordinator in Liberia
a6595.name: Christine N. Umutoni
a6595.title: UN Resident Coordinator in Liberia
a6595.speech: Informed Foreign Minister Nyanti about an upcoming retreat with all development partners in Liberia, scheduled for April 17, 2025, and extended an invitation for her participation.

a6595.speaker: Christine N. Umutoni, UN Resident Coordinator in Liberia
a6595.name: Christine N. Umutoni
a6595.title: UN Resident Coordinator in Liberia
a6595.speech: While acknowledging that some UN agencies in Liberia have experienced a freeze in recruitment, stressed that the UN is aware of the challenges posed by this decision and its impact on implementing the ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development (AAID), despite these challenges.

a6595.speaker: UN Country Team / UN delegation in Liberia (including UNDP, UNICEF, UNFPA, UN-Women, UNHCHR, IFAD, IOM and WFP)
a6595.name: UN Country Team / UN delegation in Liberia (including UNDP
a6595.title: UNICEF, UNFPA, UN-Women, UNHCHR, IFAD, IOM and WFP)
a6595.speech: Highlighted key progress and ongoing projects supporting Liberia's development agenda ; reaffirmed its commitment to assisting Liberia in achieving the ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development and emphasized the importance of continued support for Liberia's peacebuilding efforts, particularly in strengthening national institutions, enhancing human rights protection, and fostering social inclusion.

a6595.speaker: UN Country Team / UN delegation in Liberia
a6595.name: UN Country Team / UN delegation in Liberia
a6595.speech: Assured Foreign Minister Nyanti that Liberia's needs would continue to be prioritized in their programming ; pledged to work alongside the government to mobilize additional resources and emphasized the importance of maintaining a partnership based on sustained collaboration, transparency, and mutual respect between the UN and Liberia's government, civil society, and other stakeholders.

a6595.speaker: Sara Beysolow Nyanti, Liberia's Minister of Foreign Affairs
a6595.name: Sara Beysolow Nyanti
a6595.title: Liberia's Minister of Foreign Affairs
a6595.speech: Expressed her deep appreciation for the UN's unwavering support of Liberia's development and peace initiatives ; commended the UN for providing timely assistance and expertise, particularly during Liberia's post-conflict reconstruction period.

a6595.speaker: Sara Beysolow Nyanti, Liberia's Minister of Foreign Affairs
a6595.name: Sara Beysolow Nyanti
a6595.title: Liberia's Minister of Foreign Affairs
a6595.speech: Acknowledged the significant progress Liberia has made in its recovery and development journey but noted that challenges remain, especially in areas such as unemployment, healthcare, infrastructure, and economic diversification ; urged for increased international support, particularly in capacity building, job creation, and sustainable economic development.

a6595.speaker: Sara Beysolow Nyanti, Liberia's Minister of Foreign Affairs
a6595.name: Sara Beysolow Nyanti
a6595.title: Liberia's Minister of Foreign Affairs
a6595.speech: Emphasized the importance of continued UN-Liberia collaboration in addressing emerging challenges such as the economic impact of climate change, food security, and access to education and healthcare ; highlighted the need for the UN to remain flexible and responsive to Liberia's evolving needs, particularly in the face of global challenges like health crises and economic downturns.

a6595.speaker: Sara Beysolow Nyanti, Liberia's Minister of Foreign Affairs
a6595.name: Sara Beysolow Nyanti
a6595.title: Liberia's Minister of Foreign Affairs
a6595.speech: Called for a stronger UN presence in Liberia's rural areas, where much of the country's population resides ; advocated for a greater focus on inclusive development programs that would benefit marginalized and underserved communities.

a6843.speaker: Dr Hussein Mwinyi, President of Zanzibar
a6843.name: Dr Hussein Mwinyi
a6843.title: President of Zanzibar
a6843.speech: Called for deeper cooperation and the strengthening of economic diplomacy between Zanzibar and Japan; congratulated Amb Mutatembwa on his appointment and wished him success in his mission, stressing the importance of focusing on three key priority areas, trade, investment and development assistance: “Japan is home to many investors who could be welcomed to Zanzibar, particularly in sectors tied to the Blue Economy such as fisheries and marine products, tourism, sports, as well as oil and gas.” ; noted that the Blue Economy remains a top strategic focus for Zanzibar and stressed the need to attract more investors from Japan to support the establishment of marine product processing industries; pointed at seaweed trade as a promising sector, revealing that a Japanese company has already expressed interest in supplying a seaweed processing machine to Zanzibar, with the goal of increasing value-added production and opening up access to the Japanese market: “This marks a crucial step in diversifying our exports and promoting value-added products.”

a6843.speaker: Anderson Mutatembwa, Tanzania’s newly appointed Ambassador to Japan
a6843.name: Anderson Mutatembwa
a6843.title: Tanzania’s newly appointed Ambassador to Japan
a6843.speech: Assured the president of his commitment to exploring and securing opportunities for economic cooperation between Tanzania and Japan; said his efforts would focus on attracting projects that benefit both mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar, particularly in the areas of infrastructure, health, water and trade: “I will work diligently to build partnerships and identify areas of mutual interest that will drive development and prosperity for our people.”

a6843.speaker: Dr Hussein Mwinyi, President of Zanzibar and CCM Vice-Chairman (Zanzibar)
a6843.name: Dr Hussein Mwinyi
a6843.title: President of Zanzibar and CCM Vice-Chairman (Zanzibar)
a6843.speech: Said that the progress of the ruling party’s campaigns so far reflects strong acceptance among Tanzanians and points to victory in the upcoming elections; congratulated Dr Migiro on her appointment as the party’s chief executive and expressed confidence in her leadership abilities; welcomed the impressive turnout at CCM rallies across regions of mainland Tanzania, saying it demonstrates the party’s wide support and likelihood of winning the general elections; thanked CCM headquarters for its support to CCM Zanzibar ahead of the official launch of campaigns scheduled for Saturday in Zanzibar.

a6843.speaker: Dr Asha-Rose Migiro, CCM Secretary General
a6843.name: Dr Asha-Rose Migiro
a6843.title: CCM Secretary General
a6843.speech: Thanked CCM for the trust placed in her and pledged close collaboration with CCM Zanzibar, working shoulder-to-shoulder during the campaign season.

a6913.speaker: UNAIDS
a6913.name: UNAIDS
a6913.speech: Warned against a dramatic resurgence of the AIDS pandemic following the recent budget cuts made by the United States ; expressed its grave concern at the closure of care centres, the layoffs of medical staff and the direct impact on young African women, who are particularly vulnerable to the disease ; expects the 1.3 million new infections recorded in 2023 to explode to 8.7 million within a few years.

a6913.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, Executive Director of UNAIDS
a6913.name: Winnie Byanyima
a6913.title: Executive Director of UNAIDS
a6913.speech: Said that without a return of American aid or alternative funding, 6.3 million additional AIDS-related deaths could occur over the next four years, ten times higher than the 600,000 deaths estimated in 2023 ; "If the situation does not change, we risk losing the progress made over the past 25 years," she added at a press briefing in Geneva, Switzerland.

a6913.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, Executive Director of UNAIDS
a6913.name: Winnie Byanyima
a6913.title: Executive Director of UNAIDS
a6913.speech: Made a direct appeal to the new American president, urging him to continue the HIV prevention revolution, notably by supporting the introduction of injectable doses twice a year.

a7026.speaker: Ghana AIDS Commission (GAC)
a7026.name: Ghana AIDS Commission (GAC)
a7026.speech: Has expressed concern over the declining use of condoms among young people, attributing the trend to a reduced fear of HIV and AIDS infections.

a7026.speaker: Isaiah Doe Kwao, Director of Research, Monitoring and Evaluation, Ghana AIDS Commission
a7026.name: Isaiah Doe Kwao
a7026.title: Director of Research, Monitoring and Evaluation, Ghana AIDS Commission
a7026.speech: Said that although condoms remained widely available, many young people were becoming complacent about their sexual health, opting for unprotected sex despite the risks ; “Even though we have condoms in this country, it appears the youth of today are not using them as we would want” ; explained that some young people preferred “going raw” and believed HIV was no longer deadly because there were fewer visible deaths ; “Some say they prefer the natural feel. Others think HIV is no longer deadly because they no longer see people dying like before, so the fear factor is gone” ; described such perceptions as dangerous, stressing that condoms remained one of the most effective tools for preventing HIV, STIs and unintended pregnancies ; “As much as possible, we continue to encourage them to reduce risky behaviours. Condom use is still key in preventing HIV and other infections. We advise them to either abstain, remain faithful to one partner, or use condoms consistently and correctly.”

a7026.speaker: Isaiah Doe Kwao, Director of Research, Monitoring and Evaluation, Ghana AIDS Commission
a7026.name: Isaiah Doe Kwao
a7026.title: Director of Research, Monitoring and Evaluation, Ghana AIDS Commission
a7026.speech: Urged young people to take their health seriously, noting that their wellbeing was vital to Ghana's future development ; “The youth are the future leaders of this country. We want them to stay safe, grow into healthy adults, and contribute meaningfully to national development.”

a7026.speaker: Isaiah Doe Kwao, Director of Research, Monitoring and Evaluation, Ghana AIDS Commission
a7026.name: Isaiah Doe Kwao
a7026.title: Director of Research, Monitoring and Evaluation, Ghana AIDS Commission
a7026.speech: On Ghana's goal of ending AIDS by 2030, said the Commission was developing a strategic plan (2026–2030) to guide interventions towards achieving the global 95-95-95 targets, which would ensure that all persons living with HIV know their status, receive treatment and achieve viral suppression.

a7026.speaker: Isaiah Doe Kwao, Director of Research, Monitoring and Evaluation, Ghana AIDS Commission
a7026.name: Isaiah Doe Kwao
a7026.title: Director of Research, Monitoring and Evaluation, Ghana AIDS Commission
a7026.speech: Noted that inadequate funding remained a major challenge following the withdrawal or reduction of support from donor partners such as USAID and the Global Fund ; “It is incumbent on the government of Ghana to fill in the gap so that we can implement the interventions we've laid out” ; also appealed to the private sector to support the national HIV response through corporate social responsibility initiatives and contributions to the Ghana HIV and AIDS Fund ; “We have developed a short code, *9898#, where individuals can donate as little as one cedi to support HIV activities in the country.”

a7026.speaker: Kakra Essamuah, Board Chair of the Ghana AIDS Commission and Chairperson of the event
a7026.name: Kakra Essamuah
a7026.title: Board Chair of the Ghana AIDS Commission and Chairperson of the event
a7026.speech: Said the Commission remained committed to mobilising domestic resources to sustain Ghana's HIV response and eliminate AIDS as a public health threat by 2030; commended stakeholders for their continued collaboration and called for renewed commitment and innovation to address emerging challenges in the national HIV response.

a7026.speaker: Representatives from UNESCO, the Global Fund, NAP+ Ghana and the Ghana Employers Association
a7026.name: Representatives from UNESCO
a7026.title: the Global Fund, NAP+ Ghana and the Ghana Employers Association
a7026.speech: Pledged continued support to Ghana's efforts in combating HIV and AIDS.

a7113.speaker: Jacqueline Musiitwa, USAID Deputy Assistant Administrator
a7113.name: Jacqueline Musiitwa
a7113.title: USAID Deputy Assistant Administrator
a7113.speech: Announced one million US dollars in emergency aid to support Niger, hard hit by the recent floods, during a working visit to Niamey ; in her announcement she highlighted the importance of international aid and of global partnership in overcoming natural challenges and strengthening the resilience of communities; she also expressed her compassion and support for the affected families, assuring that USAID would work tirelessly to provide the necessary assistance and to support Niger in its recovery and development efforts.

a7113.speaker: US Embassy in Niger (press statement)
a7113.name: US Embassy in Niger (press statement)
a7113.speech: Made the announcement of the one-million-dollar emergency aid public on Monday.

a7113.speaker: USAID and development and humanitarian partners (joint commitments at meetings in Niamey)
a7113.name: USAID and development and humanitarian partners (joint commitments at meetings in Niamey)
a7113.speech: The various parties committed to intensifying their cooperation to address the challenges linked to climate change and to improve the resilience of the most vulnerable communities in Niger.

a7113.speaker: International community
a7113.name: International community
a7113.speech: The declaration of this American assistance follows a call by the international community to step up efforts to support vulnerable countries facing the effects of climate change.

a7238.speaker: Managers of the Rossing and Husab uranium mines (Namibia)
a7238.name: Managers of the Rossing and Husab uranium mines (Namibia)
a7238.speech: Say the advancement in technology could make it possible for Namibia to add value, but they questioned what measures the government will put in place to ensure that the requirement is met.

a7238.speaker: Tjekero Tweya, Member of Parliament (Namibia)
a7238.name: Tjekero Tweya
a7238.title: Member of Parliament (Namibia)
a7238.speech: Asked the managers of Rossing and Husab Uranium mines if they were scared of the government's ban on exports of critical raw materials; the lawmakers wanted to know if there was a possibility of exporting a finished product.

a7238.speaker: Shaan van Schalkwyk, Chief Financial Officer at CNNC Rossing Uranium
a7238.name: Shaan van Schalkwyk
a7238.title: Chief Financial Officer at CNNC Rossing Uranium
a7238.speech: Explained that "the next step is conversion, and I share with your view that even if you convert in a different country and the next stage, after that comes a step that also happens at another facility, but in the end, you know nuclear power is the future, and there is certainly technology coming on the market that modularizes nuclear power so that you don't have to build it as big as nuclear power used to be that you can do it in smaller modular units. And certainly, that must be something that we as Namibians must consider, even if we put up a one-gigawatt reactor in Namibia."

a7238.speaker: Irvinne Simataa, Executive Vice President at Husab Uranium
a7238.name: Irvinne Simataa
a7238.title: Executive Vice President at Husab Uranium
a7238.speech: Informed the parliamentarians "We are not afraid of that; we just ask the question: What is the government putting in place to ensure that such beneficiation as intended becomes a reality? I'm talking about infrastructure; I'm talking about training of resources; I'm talking about technology."

a7298.speaker: Rachelle R. Kanneh, journalist, Voice of Gbarpolu, winner of the 2nd Young Journalist Award
a7298.name: Rachelle R. Kanneh
a7298.title: journalist, Voice of Gbarpolu, winner of the 2nd Young Journalist Award
a7298.speech: “As a woman in a field often dominated by men, I strive to bring a unique perspective, emphasizing issues that affect marginalized communities, women and families.”

a7323.speaker: European Union and its member States (statement)
a7323.name: European Union and its member States (statement)
a7323.speech: Following the state of national catastrophe declared in Mali on 23 August, the EU and its member States demonstrate their support by mobilising to date more than 3 billion CFA francs in additional humanitarian assistance for the populations most affected by the devastating floods; they state they continue to follow closely the emergency situation caused by the floods in several regions of Mali and continue to provide assistance to the Malian population during this difficult period, and that they are leading donors to the humanitarian response provided by the United Nations agencies.

a7427.speaker: Inside sources (anonymous)
a7427.name: Inside sources (anonymous)
a7427.speech: According to inside sources, each truck reportedly pays no less than USD 30 per discharge, with an estimated 19 to 20 trucks making multiple dumps daily; any truck exceeding this number of dumps is required to pay an additional equivalent amount at the LWSC administrative building on Water Street.

a7427.speaker: Vacuum truck driver (anonymous)
a7427.name: Vacuum truck driver (anonymous)
a7427.speech: Confirmed to our reporters in a phone call interview that the information is accurate and that they are indeed doing business with LWSC; said some of his colleagues don’t always manage the waste properly by tightening the bolt holds, and as a result it often leaks: “I will talk to you, but I don’t want my name mentioned because I’m working for someone else, and it might look like I’m spoiling their business. I’m a driver, and we usually dump the waste in the Water and Sewer yard. But sometimes, some of the guys don’t do a proper job, they don’t tighten the bolt holds, and as a result, the sewage leaks out, even the LWSC Pupu truck can do the same thing.” ; “But what can I do? I just see it and pass. There are people responsible for stopping them. For example, if I tell someone what they’re doing is wrong, they’ll say I like to cause confusion or that I’m trying to act like a government official. So, I just pass and mind my business.”

a7427.speaker: Residents of the surrounding community
a7427.name: Residents of the surrounding community
a7427.speech: In an interview with residents, the surrounding community reported a persistent foul odor, skin infections, malaria outbreaks, and suspected water contamination, conditions they believe are linked to the dumping activities.

a7427.speaker: James F. Cooper, member of the Elder Council representing the three affected communities
a7427.name: James F. Cooper
a7427.title: member of the Elder Council representing the three affected communities
a7427.speech: “The smell is constant. We are suffering here. We only want the government to please relocate the two facilities that are polluting the community. It’s unsafe for the over 600 to 700 houses that are located here. When the rain falls, you’ll see ‘pupu’ (feces) floating on the water. It even enters our houses at times” ; appealed to the government to come to their aid and find a new location for the sewage facility, as their condition continues to worsen ; “You see, we can put sandbags in front of our houses, to stop water from entering our houses. During heavy rainfall, this place gets flooded” ; noted that sometimes water still enters their houses ; told The New Dawn that community leaders have reached out to the LWSC administration, even Managing Director Mo Ali, to discuss the situation, but the response has remained the same ; revealed that some residents working with LWSC are afraid to speak out for fear of losing their jobs.

a7427.speaker: Mo Ali, Managing Director, Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation (LWSC)
a7427.name: Mo Ali
a7427.title: Managing Director, Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation (LWSC)
a7427.speech: Was allegedly quoted as saying, “They never asked us to live there.”

a7427.speaker: Mo Ali, Managing Director, Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation (LWSC)
a7427.name: Mo Ali
a7427.title: Managing Director, Liberia Water and Sewer Corporation (LWSC)
a7427.speech: When contacted via WhatsApp for comment, did not provide a formal response, but rather stated: “LOL. Do you have any idea who is responsible for receiving sewage from commercial sewer trucks? Do you think it is free to treat the sewage LWSC gets from commercial sewage operators? Tell me, what exactly do you want? Because I’m not sure this is the real thing you want to talk about. Do you know the functions of LWSC? I would appreciate it if next time you did your investigation to uncover,’ you would also read the Act that established LWSC. Have a great day.” ; when questioned about the reported violation of Liberia’s Environmental Protection and Management Law, he simply responded, “Okay,” offering no further comment.

a7427.speaker: Annie Kollie, a resident
a7427.name: Annie Kollie
a7427.title: a resident
a7427.speech: Expressed her frustration: “We smell it every day. When it rains, the waste flows through the alleys and into our homes. Our children are constantly sick with rashes and diarrhea, but no one from the government ever comes here to explain anything.” ; according to her, on July 26th the Monrovia City Corporation (MCC), which also operates a primary dumpsite in the heart of the community, held a party where community leaders were invited, but nothing ever changes.

a7427.speaker: Health workers in the surrounding area
a7427.name: Health workers in the surrounding area
a7427.speech: While some believe the illnesses may be linked to the situation, others say it could also be due to the fact that many residents drink from hand pumps and wells, which are not safe.

a7427.speaker: Phere M. Beangar, health worker at the God’s Grace Medicine Store
a7427.name: Phere M. Beangar
a7427.title: health worker at the God’s Grace Medicine Store
a7427.speech: Confirmed that they are unsure whether some of the cases are linked to the situation: “I sometimes receive patients with illnesses such as typhoid, skin infections, cholera, malaria, and fever” ; according to him, some customers simply buy medicine and treat themselves at home: ‘I can’t say for sure whether their illnesses are linked to what you’re talking about.’

a7427.speaker: World Health Organization (guidelines)
a7427.name: World Health Organization (guidelines)
a7427.speech: According to the World Health Organization’s guidelines, the air quality in Liberia is considered moderately unsafe; the WHO guidelines indicate that air pollution is the single most significant contributor to the adverse health effects in Liberia, causing an estimated 3,900 premature deaths every year.

a7427.speaker: Sources within LWSC (anonymous)
a7427.name: Sources within LWSC (anonymous)
a7427.speech: Told The NewDawn that during the Ebola crisis, the Fiamah facility was used by LWSC, UNMIL, and other private sewer operators, and was also used to transfer Ebola-contaminated liquid waste from various ETU centers.

a7427.speaker: Public health authorities (2017)
a7427.name: Public health authorities (2017)
a7427.speech: Warned at the time that, due to the nonfunctional state of the Fiamah Treatment Plant, wastewater volumes would rise, and as a result large sections of Liberia’s population would be dangerously exposed to unsafe water and sanitation, posing a serious threat to national public health standards.

a7427.speaker: Environmental Protection and Management Law of Liberia (Section 59)
a7427.name: Environmental Protection and Management Law of Liberia (Section 59)
a7427.speech: “No person shall discard, dump, or leave any litter on any land, coastal zone, or water surface, street, road, or site in or on any place to which the public has access, except in a container or at a place which has been specially indicated, provided, or set apart for such purpose. Every person or authority in control of or responsible for the maintenance of any place to which the public has access shall at all times ensure that containers or places are provided which will normally be adequate.” It further states: “A person who discharges, discards, dumps or leaves any litter on any land, coastal zone or water surface, street, road or site or in or on any place in the environment contrary to subsection (1) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding US $5,000 or to imprisonment for a period not exceeding one year or to both. Any person who contravenes the provisions of this section shall be required to undertake community service and clean up the litter using the best available methods, taking precautions to protect human health and the environment.”

a7427.speaker: Executive Director of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) of Liberia
a7427.name: Executive Director of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) of Liberia
a7427.speech: In a brief phone call and WhatsApp interview, said he was attending an official function after a set of questions and images were sent to him; he promised to return the call, but weeks later has yet to follow up and remains unresponsive to repeated phone calls and WhatsApp messages.

a7479.speaker: well-informed sources (anonymous)
a7479.name: well-informed sources (anonymous)
a7479.speech: According to well-informed sources, the Central African head of state also had a separate meeting with Kaja Kallas, the EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs, dominated by the case of Martin Joseph Figueira, an employee of the American NGO FHI 360 imprisoned in the CAR since May 2024.

a7479.speaker: Member of the Central African delegation present during the discussions (anonymous)
a7479.name: Member of the Central African delegation present during the discussions (anonymous)
a7479.speech: Said that Kaja Kallas adopted a hard tone, accompanying her demand with explicit threats, and that President Touadera refused, insisting on his country's legal sovereignty.

a7479.speaker: Kaja Kallas, EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs
a7479.name: Kaja Kallas
a7479.title: EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs
a7479.speech: Is said to have adopted a hard tone in demanding the release of Martin Joseph Figueira, accompanying her demand with explicit threats.

a7479.speaker: Faustin-Archange Touadera, President of the Central African Republic
a7479.name: Faustin-Archange Touadera
a7479.title: President of the Central African Republic
a7479.speech: “Central African justice is conducted in complete independence, without any external influence” ; “If the evidence confirms Mr Figueira's guilt, he will suffer the consequences in accordance with our laws.”

a7479.speaker: Faustin-Archange Touadera, President of the Central African Republic
a7479.name: Faustin-Archange Touadera
a7479.title: President of the Central African Republic
a7479.speech: Firmly affirmed that the era of unilateral European diktats over Africa was over: “The Central African Republic accepts no ultimatum. We have circumvented sanctions in the past and we will once again keep our dignity while building alliances with partners who respect our independence.”
